citation: Wang H, Heijnen CJ, Eijkelkamp N, Garza Carbajal A, Schedlowski M, Kelley KW, Dantzer R, Kavelaars A. GRK2 in sensory neurons regulates epinephrine-induced signalling and duration of mechanical hyperalgesia. Pain 2011;152(7):1649-1658
text_quality: ok (all 10 PDF pages, references complete; extraction loses the superscript minus of genotypes, so GRK2+/- reads as 'GRK2+/ ' and GRK2-/- as 'GRK2 / ', renders the micro-litre unit as 'lL', PKC-epsilon as 'PKCe' and Greek beta/alpha as 'b'/'a')
design: Controlled laboratory experiments in mice: genotype comparisons (wild-type littermates versus global, cell-specific and tamoxifen-inducible GRK2-deficient lines) and pretreatment comparisons with receptor and kinase inhibitors against vehicle. Repeated-measures behavioural time courses, plus Western blotting and immunohistochemistry. The experimenter was blinded to genotype and treatment.
population: Male and female C57BL/6 mice aged 12 to 14 weeks: wild-type littermates; global GRK2+/-; sensory-neuron-specific SNS-GRK2+/- (Nav1.8-Cre); microglia/macrophage-specific LysM-GRK2+/-; astrocyte-specific GFAP-GRK2+/-; tamoxifen-inducible TAM-GRK2+/- and TAM-GRK2-/-. After the first experiment showed the same effect in both sexes, only female mice were used.
n: n = 8/group for the mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia time courses (including the tamoxifen-inducible, SNS, LysM and GFAP experiments); n = 4-6/group for the adrenoceptor-blocker experiments; n = 6-8/group for the PKA, PKCe and MEK inhibitor experiments; n = 3-4/group for Western blots and for DRG morphology (based on more than 500 neurons per mouse)
setting: Animal facility of the University of Utrecht, the Netherlands; approved by the University Medical Center Utrecht experimental animal committee
intervention: A single intraplantar injection of epinephrine ([dose figure omitted]) into the hind paw. In separate experiments the alpha-adrenoceptor blocker phentolamine, the beta2-adrenoceptor blocker ICI-118,551, the PKA inhibitor H-89, the PKCe inhibitor TAT-PKCev1-2 or the MEK/ERK inhibitor U0126 was injected intraplantarly 30 minutes before the epinephrine injection. A second, lower epinephrine amount was used in one mechanical-hyperalgesia experiment in female mice.
comparator: Wild-type (or Cre-negative GRK2+/+) littermates for every genotype comparison; saline, scrambled TAT-PKCev1-2 or vehicle for every inhibitor comparison
route: Intraplantar injection into the hind paw (not intradermal, and not into the paw dorsum); inhibitors by the same route; tamoxifen intraperitoneally
duration: One injection, then repeated testing from 0.5 hours through about 21 days
outcomes: Mechanical hyperalgesia as the change in the 50% paw withdrawal threshold (von Frey hairs, up-and-down method); thermal hyperalgesia as heat withdrawal latency (Hargreaves test); GRK2 protein in dorsal root ganglia, spinal cord and peritoneal macrophages by Western blot; dorsal root ganglion neuron size distribution and percentage of IB4-positive neurons by immunohistochemistry

key_results.quote: We demonstrate for the first time that EPI-induced mechanical as well as thermal hyperalgesia is prolonged to approximately 21 days in GRK2+/ mice, whereas it lasts only 3 to 4 days in wild-type mice.
A total volume of [dose figure omitted] EPI per paw was injected intraplantarly to induce hyperalgesia.
The experimenter was blinded for genotype and treatment during all measurements.
In GRK2+/ mice, EPI-induced hyperalgesia lasted approximately 21 days vs 3 to 4 days in WT mice (Fig. 1A and B).
In male and female WT mice, EPI-induced thermal hyperalgesia lasted 3 to 4 days.

At a low dose of EPI ([dose figure omitted]), mechanical hyperalgesia also lasted longer in GRK2+/ than in WT mice (Fig. 1C). In addition, at this low dose of EPI, acute hyperalgesia was increased in GRK2+/ mice.

EPI-induced mechanical hyperalgesia was slightly but significantly enhanced in SNS-GRK2+/ mice (Fig. 5A), and lasted approximately 21 days. Mechanical hyperalgesia in control littermates returned to baseline levels within 4 days.

In both WT (Fig. 4A) and GRK2+/ (Fig. 4B) mice, the b2-AR blocker inhibited EPI-induced hyperalgesia. In contrast, the a-AR blocker, phentolamine, had no effect on EPI-induced hyperalgesia in both genotypes.
These findings indicate that low GRK2 may shift the dose-response curve for EPI to the left.
Thus, our present findings confirm and expand further the emerging scenario that low nociceptor GRK2 induces a switch in cAMP signalling from PKA- toward PKCe-dependent pathways.
We did not observe any genotype-related difference in the percentage of IB4+ and IB4- small-diameter neurons that are thought to be important for inflammatory hyperalgesia.

author_limitations.quote: However, we cannot completely exclude that other AR subtypes also contribute partially to EPI-induced hyperalgesia in both genotypes.
However, no data are available on the contribution of low GRK2 to the development of DRG neurons.
Whether in conditions of low GRK2 MEK/ERK becomes part of the signalling complex with (Epac-)PKCe or MEK/ERK activation occurs as part of a separate signalling route remains to be established.

These apparent differences in the use of PKA may be due to species differences (rat versus mouse), the way mechanical threshold was analysed (von Frey versus Randall-Selito test), and/or the use of different PKA inhibitors (H89 versus the peptide inhibitor WIPTIDE).

Dorn 2nd (Washington University) for sharing the GRK2-fLox mice, and a technician. Conflicts: "The authors have no conflicts of interest related to this study." (PDF p. 9)

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Khasar SG, McCarter G, Levine JD. Epinephrine produces a beta-adrenergic receptor-mediated mechanical hyperalgesia and in vitro sensitization of rat nociceptors. J Neurophysiol 1999;81:1104-12 (ref [18])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: The rat study the Lidocaine With Epinephrine Wheals page's two-hour window comes from (claim C090). Wang cites it for local epinephrine inducing transient thermal and mechanical hyperalgesia. Its abstract reports an intradermal injection into the dorsum of the rat hindpaw, a dose-dependent mechanical hyperalgesia by the Randall-Selitto test, and hyperalgesia that lasted 2 h - so the two-hour figure is correctly attributed, but the study was not run at a single epinephrine amount.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Khasar SG, Dina OA, Green PG, Levine JD. Sound stress-induced long-term enhancement of mechanical hyperalgesia in rats is maintained by sympathoadrenal catecholamines. J Pain 2009;10:1073-7 (ref [17])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: Stress, catecholamines and pain: epinephrine-induced cutaneous and muscle hyperalgesia enhanced for up to 28 days after sound stress, maintained by circulating epinephrine. Bears on any claim that the duration of epinephrine-related hyperalgesia has not been measured since 1999.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Dina OA, Aley KO, Isenberg W, Messing RO, Levine JD. Sex hormones regulate the contribution of PKCepsilon and PKA signalling in inflammatory pain in the rat. Eur J Neurosci 2001;13:2227-33 (ref [4])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: A further Levine-group study of epinephrine-induced mechanical hyperalgesia in rats and PKCepsilon-knockout mice, with the PKA/PKCepsilon/MEK signalling and a sex difference. Wang discusses it directly as the earlier account of the signalling routes for epinephrine mechanical hyperalgesia.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Hucho TB, Dina OA, Levine JD. Epac mediates a cAMP-to-PKC signaling in inflammatory pain: an isolectin B4(+) neuron-specific mechanism. J Neurosci 2005;25:6119-26 (ref [12])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: cAMP to Epac to PKCepsilon in IB4-positive nociceptors; cited by Wang both for beta2-adrenoceptors mediating epinephrine hyperalgesia in rats and for the Epac step. Bears on nociceptor sensitisation mechanism statements.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Eijkelkamp N, Heijnen CJ, Willemen HL, et al. GRK2: a novel cell-specific regulator of severity and duration of inflammatory pain. J Neurosci 2010;30:2138-49 (ref [5])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: The companion finding that the duration of inflammatory hyperalgesia depends on the cellular level of GRK2 - the general 'duration depends on the state of the nociceptor' result behind this paper.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Eijkelkamp N, Wang H, Garza-Carbajal A, et al. Low nociceptor GRK2 prolongs prostaglandin E2 hyperalgesia via biased cAMP signalling to Epac/Rap1, protein kinase Ce, and MEK/ERK. J Neurosci 2010;30:12806-15 (ref [6])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: Same mechanism for PGE2 hyperalgesia; also the source for GRK2 being downregulated in dorsal root ganglion neurons during chronic inflammation, which is the paper's translational argument.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Willemen HL, Eijkelkamp N, Wang H, et al. Microglial/macrophage GRK2 determines duration of peripheral IL-1beta-induced hyperalgesia: contribution of spinal cord CX3CR1, p38 and IL-1 signalling. Pain 2010;150:550-60 (ref [34])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: Another measurement of how long peripherally induced hyperalgesia lasts and what sets that duration; relevant wherever a page treats the length of a sensitisation window as a fixed property.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Kleibeuker W, Ledeboer A, Eijkelkamp N, et al. A role for G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 in mechanical allodynia. Eur J Neurosci 2007;25:1696-704 (ref [19])
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: GRK2 and mechanical allodynia; part of the same series on what determines the duration and intensity of mechanical hypersensitivity.
